extra: Bytes written by the packed payload
Bytes written by the packed payload

comments.text: Disables interrupts and the display, installs the ending IRQ at line $10, sets up six sprites and configures VIC bank $C000 for the bitmap presentation. Copies graphics under the I/O area before restoring $01 to $35.
Begin the blanked-display setup immediately after SEI.
Immediate $0B for the first write to the VIC vertical control register.
Blank the screen before changing the ending's raster interrupt.
Low operand byte of the $D011 store at $9083.
High operand byte of the $D011 store. The following loads pass raster line $10 and the vector low byte $96.
Load the vector high byte $91 before storing the raster line.
High operand byte of the $D012 store. The next instruction installs the vector low byte at $FFFE.
Low operand byte of the $FFFE store. The following STY installs the vector high byte at $FFFF.
Low operand byte of the $FFFF vector store at $9092.
High operand byte of the same vector store. Initialization of the cylinder coordinates begins at $9095.
Initializes the cylinder coordinates, enables six multicolour sprites, and selects the bank-$C000 bitmap display before the scene copies.

Opens RAM under I/O. Copies bitmap rows from $D000 and $B800 into $E800–$FEFF, then copies the final 64-byte slice from $BF00 to $FF00. Moves the bank-$C000 workspace, restores I/O, and enters the colour-cell copy.
Copies four overlapping source slices beginning at $B3E8 to the C64 colour-RAM window after restoring access to I/O.
Clears the ending sequence counters and background colours, sets up the text display state and starts the music through $5500 with selector one. Enables interrupts before making the scene visible.
Waits for the IRQ-side code to set $955A before running the fixed delay loops and moving to the next ending phase.
Column within the current six-glyph laboratory sprite strip. The IRQ multiplies it by eight to form the glyph destination.
Index into the split destination tables at $95C7 and $95CC for laboratory message glyphs.
Half-resolution X coordinate copied into the first two lower multiplexed sprites, with the right-hand sprite offset by 12 before doubling.
Y coordinate for the first row of the lower multiplexed sprites. The other row is placed 20 pixels lower.
Flag written by the $9164 and $9167 entries. The ending IRQs use it to select blanked or visible display values for $D011.
Sets the visible flag at $9163 through the shared following code, then waits for two IRQ acknowledgments through $59.
Clears the visible flag at $9163, then uses the same two acknowledgments.
Copies X complete pages from source high byte A to destination high byte Y. Patches both high-byte operands and increments them after each 256-byte copy.
High byte of the $9183 source operand. The page-copy entry installs it from A.
High byte of the $9186 destination operand. The copier installs it from Y and increments both page operands after each 256-byte transfer.
First raster handler installed at $908F-$9092.
Restore Y from $05 before returning from the raster interrupt.
Clears the display acknowledgment, changes the common sprite colours, and builds four sprite coordinates from a base position at $9161/$9162 before writing their pointers and VIC registers.

Immediate byte of the load at $923F. When nonzero, the IRQ decrements it before choosing the lower sprite pointers. It then writes positions, pointer bytes and colours for four sprites, updates the laboratory sequence, and schedules the next raster interrupt.
Every fourth call after the laboratory message ends, move one pair of sprite Y positions up by two toward its limit. Once both pairs reach their limits the scene can finish.
Low operand byte of the store that moves the second sprite in the selected pair to the new Y coordinate.
Low operand byte of the absolute load at $92FF. Its effective address is $94F6, the initial Y entry for the second sprite pair.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $9307, selecting offset two for updates to the second pair of Y positions.
Countdown reloaded with three before each exit-animation step.
First pair's target Y, compared at $92EE.
Second pair's target Y, compared at $9302.
Decrements the sprite-frame update divider and returns until it underflows.
Reloads the divider, then toggles the immediate byte at $931E to select alternate frame states.
Immediate operand of the load at $931D, toggled between zero and one with EOR.
Immediate mask of the EOR at $931F. The result selects one of two countdowns and sprite pointer destinations.
XORs two bitmap bytes from $E000 and $E800 at the same offset. The caller uses bit zero to choose the direction of the frame update.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $9359. Incremented once per sample so successive calls use different bitmap offsets.
Toggled by a $FE command in the message stream. When set, the IRQ checks the cylinder animation before advancing the glyph sequence.
Countdown checked before producing the next glyph. The $FE command loads $70 here.
Countdown for updates to the two lower sprite pointer bytes. The $9318 path reloads it with one.
Two offsets added to $2A to produce the pair of frame pointers at $94FE.
Reloads the blink divider on underflow, toggles a flag and changes the sixth byte of the current glyph.
Immediate value toggled by EOR at $9376 to select between the two glyph-byte writes.
Writes zero to byte five of the active glyph when called at $937D. The alternate entry at $9380 writes $3F.
Reads the current glyph index from $9463, shifts it by three and patches the absolute source at $93AB. Index $1B uses the blank-marker path.
Low byte of the $93AB operand, patched with the glyph offset plus the base low byte $FC.
High byte of the glyph source operand. The copy transfers eight bytes to ($0F), then advances the column and rolls it into the next strip at column six.
Reads the next message item at $9563. Zero sets $9559, $FE toggles an animation bit and continues fetching, space maps to $1C, and $FF maps to $1B. The selected glyph index is masked to six bits.
Immediate Y operand at $93D4. The stream reader sets the exit flag on zero, handles $FE as a timed mode toggle, and translates $FF to glyph $1B.
Copies four strips of 48 bytes to the preceding strip positions, advancing both pointers by $140 between copies. Clears the source of the final copy.
Defers movement while $9240 is nonzero. Otherwise clears the count of matching coordinates and compares both positions with their destinations.

Immediate byte of the LDY at $9462. After decrementing Y, the code compares the two position bytes at $9161 and $9162 against their indexed destinations at $94B6 and $94D2. A coordinate that differs moves by two toward its destination. If both comparisons match, the routine sets the frame countdown to $10 and returns with carry set.
Counts coordinates already equal to their targets. Two matches set the frame countdown and return carry set.
Starts at three for the four strip copies and underflows before the last source strip is cleared.
Countdown reloaded with $0E before toggling byte five of the active glyph.
First position byte target for each indexed step of the laboratory animation. The comparison at $9468 selects it.
Second position byte target for each indexed step of the laboratory animation. The comparison at $9487 selects it.
Six low X coordinates read by the laboratory scene IRQ at $91BC. The carry from doubling them supplies the high X bit.
Six Y coordinates read at $91CE. The sequence updates the cylinder sprites by changing these values at $92F8.
Y coordinate of the other sprite in the first pair, written alongside its partner at $94F4.
Y coordinates for the second pair moving up during the exit, then for the other two top sprites.
VIC pointer values for the upper sprites indexed at $91D4. The sequence updates the last two entries at $9355.
Two sprite frame pointers derived from the offsets at $9368 and $9369 by adding $2A.
Six individual sprite colours transferred to the VIC colour registers at $91DA.
Four low X coordinates derived from $9161, doubled by $926D before writing the VIC.
X coordinate of the upper-right sprite in half-pixel units, set by adding 12 to $9161.
X coordinate of the lower-left sprite, also copied directly from $9161.
X coordinate of the lower-right sprite, also set 12 half-resolution coordinate units to the right.
Four Y coordinates derived from $9162 before the lower-burst sprite transfer.
Y coordinate of the upper-right sprite, copied directly from $9162.
Y coordinate of the lower-left sprite, set 20 pixels below $9162.
Y coordinate of the lower-right sprite, equal to the one at $950C.
Four VIC sprite pointers built from the alternate poses beginning at $38 or $3A.
Pointer for the upper-right sprite, one greater than the upper-left pointer.
Pointer for the lower-left sprite, three greater than the upper-right pointer.
Pointer for the lower-right sprite, one greater than the lower-left pointer.
Four lower sprite colours read at $9288 and stored in the VIC.
Iterates through five text areas selected by pointer tables at $95C7 and $95CC and clears 48 bytes at each. Also prepares the VIC colour entries using a self-modified address.
Low operand byte in the colour store at $953F, initialized to $D9.
High operand byte in the colour store, initialized to $D8. The loop writes six values then advances the operand by 40 for the next row.
Set on the stream terminator. Changes both the animation-frame update and the sprite exit path.
Flag polled by the main thread before it blanks the laboratory and jumps to the epilogue.
Masks used by $91C8 and $9276 to set an individual sprite's high X bit.
Character and control bytes consumed at $93D6. $FE toggles the animation bit and continues, while zero signals the message end.
Continuation of the laboratory glyph commands. Contains the later timed $FE markers and the zero terminator before the strip pointer tables.
Low bytes of five glyph strip addresses. The IRQ adds eight times the glyph column to the selected address.
Remaining low bytes of the laboratory glyph strip addresses, indexed with $9160.
High bytes of the same five glyph strip addresses. The IRQ adds the carry from the column offset.
Remaining high bytes of the laboratory glyph strip addresses used by the scroll copy.
Installs the IRQ at $96BB and disables sprites. Clears bitmap RAM backwards beginning at $FF3F before selecting entries from the scene tables.
Low byte of the destination operand at $95F3, decremented in the descending bitmap clear loop.
High byte of the bitmap clear operand. The loop exits after it underflows below $DF.
Reads a bitmap destination from $995A and a screen cell destination from $996C. The following loops copy nine strips, advancing all three source operands after each one.

Immediate strip index in the load at $9611. Twice this index selects the destination address pair. After the bitmap and attribute copies, the code increments the operand and stops when it reaches nine.
Copies 208 bytes for one row of 26 bitmap cells. Y counts from $D0 down to 1, so both patched operands start one byte before the row.
Low byte of the bitmap source operand at $9637, advanced by $D0 after each strip.
High byte of the same operand, incremented on wrap. The loop counts down from $D0 to one.
Low destination operand of the bitmap store at $963A, installed from $995A plus the strip offset.
High destination operand from $995B plus the strip offset. After the bitmap strip the initializer sets up a 26-cell attribute and colour loop.
Copies 26 bitmap attribute bytes and 26 colour RAM values for one row. The loop starts at Y=$19 and includes Y=0.
Low byte in the screen-attribute load at $9642, advanced by $1A per strip.
High byte in the same screen-attribute load. The initializer counts from 25 down to zero for each strip.
Low byte in the screen-attribute store at $9645, shared with the colour destination.
High byte in the screen-attribute store, installed from $996D plus the strip offset.
Low byte in the colour source at $9648, advanced by $1A per strip.
High byte in the colour source at $9648. The initial operand points at $AF16.
Low byte of the colour RAM store at $964B, set from the screen row address table.

High byte of the colour RAM store operand at $964B. The setup at $962A derives it from the screen attribute destination high byte by setting bits 3 and 4. The tail advances the three source operands by one row each.
Clears the text area, draws the message at $9752 and makes the scene visible. Waits for joystick fire via CIA port A before restoring the saved VIC workspace.
Selects VIC bank zero and the text display, clears the IRQ handshake byte at $59 and ticks the music player. The next interrupt is at line $72.
Selects VIC bank $C000 and bitmap mode below the text. Updates the bottom colour strip from the cycling table at $9747 and schedules the next interrupt at line $C2.
Immediate Y operand at $9730. The IRQ cycles it down through the eleven-entry colour table and uses the selected value for 23 cells at $DBC9.
The colour index decrements after this IRQ countdown underflows and reloads with three.
Eleven colours selected at $9732 to cycle the colour of 23 cells at $DBC9.
ASCII message drawn at $0400. $FF starts a new line and zero stops the reader at $9921.
Text stream continuation covering Pearly's appeal. Bytes with bit seven set advance the renderer to the next screen row.
Tail of the text stream containing the instruction to press fire and the zero that stops the renderer at $9924.
Clears 1000 screen cells beginning at $0400 and sets three 160-byte colour spans to 1.
Converts ASCII to screen codes on the 40-column screen at $0400. The high-bit marker moves the cursor to the end of the row and zero ends the stream.
Low byte of the string pointer in the load at $9921. The renderer installs it from X.
High byte of the string pointer at $9921, initialized from Y and incremented on index wrap.
Low byte of the current screen row operand in the store at $993A.
High byte of the current row operand. The renderer tests for end-of-string, treats high-bit bytes as row breaks, and advances the destination by 40 cells each row.
Nine little-endian bitmap destinations, one byte before the start of each 26-cell strip.
High byte of the first bitmap destination, followed by eight more low/high pairs read by the $9615 and $961B loads.
Nine little-endian screen attribute destinations. The row starts at column seven and successive rows are 40 cells apart.
High byte of the first screen-attribute destination, followed by eight more low/high pairs shared by the attribute and colour copy.
The payload stores $33 throughout this 1024-byte block immediately after the picture destination tables. The nine strip-copy iterations use the tables at $995A and $996C.
$998C is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
The uniform $33 fill continues to the $A000 memory-map boundary.
Continuation of the $33 fill after the epilogue destination tables, across this 1024-byte block.
$A0CB is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A1A7 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A228 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A229 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.

$A22C is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A22D is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A230 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A23F is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A240 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A24F is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A307 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
Final block of $33 fill from this address through $A5FB.
$A431 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
$A497 is inside the uniform $33 fill between the epilogue destination tables and its picture data.
Base selected by the glyph index calculation at $938D. Each index addresses eight consecutive bytes copied at $93AB.
Fourth byte of glyph 5 in the eight-byte strip font based at $A5FC, followed by the next glyphs.
Third byte of glyph 13 in the source selected by $93AB, followed by glyphs at higher indices.
Third byte of glyph 21 in the laboratory font. The strip continues through glyph 27 at $A6D4.
Last byte of the laboratory font. The epilogue bitmap copy starts one byte later because its indexed read stops when Y reaches zero.
Epilogue picture row 1, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $EA38 onward.
Epilogue picture row 2, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $EB78 onward.
Epilogue bitmap row 2, byte 11 of its 208-byte strip, copied by the loop at $9637.
Epilogue picture row 3, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $ECB8 onward.
Epilogue bitmap row 3, byte 203 of its 208-byte strip, copied by the loop at $9637.
Epilogue picture row 4, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $EDF8 onward.
Epilogue picture row 5, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $EF38 onward.
Epilogue bitmap row 5, byte 187 of its 208-byte strip, copied by the loop at $9637.
Epilogue picture row 6, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $F078 onward.
Epilogue picture row 7, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $F1B8 onward.
Epilogue picture row 8, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $F2F8 onward.
Epilogue picture row 9, 26 columns. $9637 reads the bitmap bytes and the next store writes them to $F438 onward.
Epilogue picture row 1, 26 columns. $9642 reads the screen attribute bytes and the next store writes them to $C147 onward.
Epilogue picture row 2, 26 columns. $9642 reads the screen attribute bytes and the next store writes them to $C16F onward.
Epilogue picture row 3, 26 columns. $9642 reads the screen attribute bytes and the next store writes them to $C197 onward.

Epilogue picture row 9, 26 columns. $9642 reads the screen attribute bytes and the next store writes them to $C287 onward.
Epilogue picture row 1, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $D947 onward.
Epilogue picture row 2, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $D96F onward.
Epilogue picture row 3, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $D997 onward.
Epilogue picture row 4, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $D9BF onward.

Epilogue picture row 8, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $DA5F onward.
Epilogue picture row 9, 26 columns. $9648 reads the colour RAM bytes and the next store writes them to $DA87 onward.
The first 1000 bytes are the screen colour attributes for the bitmap. $90E9 copies the four pages beginning here to screen RAM at $C000.
Colour RAM source at $90F2. The copy loop writes the four spans beginning at $D800, $D900, $DA00 and $DAE8.
Laboratory colour RAM values from row 7, column 17. The loops at $90F2–$910B transfer them to the VIC colour window.
Laboratory colour RAM values from row 13, column 33. The loops at $90F2–$910B transfer them to the VIC colour window.
Laboratory colour RAM values from row 19, column 25. The loops at $90F2–$910B transfer them to the VIC colour window.
Forty-eight $33 bytes after the 1000 colour values. The last colour transfer at $9104 reaches $B7CF.
First 1024 bytes of the bitmap slice copied from $B800 to $F800 by $90CC.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $0E7 from $B800. The copy at $90CC places this byte at $F8E7.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $277 from $B800. The copy at $90CC places this byte at $FA77.
Remainder of the bitmap source slice beginning at $B800. The last 64 bytes starting at $BF00 are copied separately at $90D1.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $407 from $B800. The copy at $90CC places this byte at $FC07.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $597 from $B800. The copy at $90CC places this byte at $FD97.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $636 from $B800. The copy at $90CC places this byte at $FE36.
Laboratory bitmap source at offset $700 from $B800. The copy at $90D1 places this byte at $FF00.
The final $B800 bitmap transfer ends at $BF3F. This block contains 192 bytes of $33 after that boundary.
Bank-$C000 sprite pointer $28 used for two upper sprites through $94FA. The VIC reads the first 63 bytes of the slot.
Pointer $29 supplies the paired overlays for the upper sprites. The VIC receives it at $91D7.
Pointer $2A begins the laboratory animation cells. $9355 replaces the last two sprite pointers as their animation advances.
Eight 64-byte sprite slots addressed by the lower IRQ's pointer sets $38/$39/$3C/$3D and $3A/$3B/$3E/$3F.
Bitmap bytes copied to $E800-$EBFF by the page-copy call at $90C3. RAM is visible beneath I/O for this transfer.
Bitmap bytes copied to $EC00-$EFFF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
Bitmap bytes copied to $F000-$F3FF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
Bitmap bytes copied to $F400-$F7FF by the page-copy call at $90C3.
First 1024 bytes at the VIC bitmap base. The scene uses these directly, before the part copied from $D000 begins at $E800.
Next 1024 bytes already at the VIC bitmap base. The scene retains these below the start of the transfer destination at $E800.

The first 1024 bytes of this loaded copy match the saved title's resident code at $7A80–$7E7F. The page-copy routine at $90C3 replaces these bytes with bitmap data from $D000 before showing the scene.
The remaining loaded copy matches title bytes $7E80–$7FFF. The same page-copy call overwrites it with the next bitmap rows.
